items.prompt: We have somatic mutations and expression for 300 head-and-neck tumours. I'd like to get something publishable out of them with network methods - any ideas?

Please use PUMA for our 85 clear-cell renal carcinomas: I want one cohort-wide network in which both transcription factors and miRNAs regulate target genes. Inputs are ready - gene-by-sample expression, a TF motif prior, a PPI file, a miRNA-target prior, and the miRNA list with one ID per line, every one of which appears in the prior's first column.

Our nutrition study has plasma metabolomics (412 features) and VST-transformed RNA-seq (2,000 genes) from the same 96 participants, with no missing values. I'd like DRAGON to fit the two-layer partial-correlation network with lambda1 fixed at 0 and lambda2 fixed at 1 - we are deliberately testing the extremes - and return the result as an edge list.
counts_norm.tsv, motif_prior.tsv and ppi_string.tsv from our 64 colon samples are in the project folder. Fire off something useful on them right now; I'll work out the actual question later.
Do the multi-omic analysis on rna_layer.csv and protein_layer.csv (same 72 patients) right away. There's no specific output in my head - just see what the two layers say together.

Across 140 breast tumours I need an estimate of how active each transcription factor is in every tumour, independent of the TF's own transcript level, together with signed TF-gene effects that separate activation from repression. I have log-normalised gene-by-sample expression, a TF-by-gene motif matrix and a TF-TF protein interaction matrix, all with matching identifiers.

In a cohort of 240 participants we measured 250 blood transcripts and 150 serum proteins on the same draws; the data are complete and continuous. What I'm after is an individual partial-correlation network for every participant linking features within and across the two layers, so I can compare them between smokers and non-smokers.
What would DRAGON tell me that GIRAFFE wouldn't? We have RNA-seq and proteomics on 60 lung adenocarcinomas and I'm trying to decide where to begin.

Set up per-sample networks on hnscc_expr.tsv (52 tumours); hs_motif.tsv and hs_ppi.tsv are in the same folder. My supervisor wrote 'one network per tumour', and it isn't clear to me whether she wants gene-gene co-expression networks or TF-to-gene regulatory networks. I'd like it running today.

I want a separate gene-gene co-expression network for each of 24 mouse hippocampus samples (12 stressed, 12 control) so I can compare per-sample gene degree between the groups. The expression matrix is gene-by-sample with a header row of sample IDs, already log2-transformed and mean-centred per gene. There are no covariates to adjust for.

Time to run LIONESS-PANDA: twins_expr.tsv holds our two monozygotic twin samples (two columns), with motif_hs.txt and ppi_hs.txt as priors. Aggregate network to twins_agg.txt, per-sample networks to lioness_twins/, started today if possible.

Splitting 210 pancreatic tumours into molecular subtypes from their RNA-seq expression is the goal: summarise genes into pathway scores, then cluster the tumours into three to five groups. Only expression data are available - there are no mutation calls for this cohort.

Can CONDOR find modules in the network a collaborator emailed me? It's a three-column weighted edge list, but I genuinely have no idea whether it's a TF-to-gene regulatory network or a gene-gene co-expression network - she only called it 'the network'.

From matched liver transcriptomics and metabolomics in 80 mice, I need to establish which metabolites causally drive the expression of lipid-metabolism genes, including the direction of each effect, for a mechanistic figure in our paper.

I'm planning to use OTTER for an aggregate TF-to-gene network from zebrafish fin RNA-seq, with a motif seed and a TF-TF PPI edge list. Honestly, I don't know yet whether we'll have one sample or two - the second library is being re-sequenced after a failed run.

Our 230 glioblastoma RNA-seq samples (about 18,000 genes) were collected at four hospitals and sequenced in two batches. The aim is to quantify how much of the gene-gene co-expression is associated with hospital and with batch, and to get an adjusted co-expression matrix out of it. The design sheet codes both covariates numerically, keyed by the same sample IDs as the expression columns.

Can OTTER be switched to computing=gpu for us? The aggregate network covers 22,000 genes and 900 TFs, CPU runs take most of a day, and our cluster has idle A100 cards. Keep every other setting at its default.

With DRAGON, I'd like three separately tuned penalties on our 110 matched colorectal tumours: lambda1 for the methylation block, lambda2 for the expression block, and a lambda_inter of 0.2 controlling only the cross-layer methylation-expression edges. Can you set it up that way?

I'm trying to understand the regulatory landscape of Arabidopsis roots under drought - about 36 RNA-seq samples, and I can get motif and protein-interaction priors. What kind of analysis makes sense here?

Sixty-four lung tumours in our biobank have matched DNA methylation, RNA expression and proteomics. I want one joint partial-correlation model that connects the features of all three layers simultaneously, not pairwise, so I can see methylation-protein links conditional on expression.

Start PANDA with expr_brain.tsv (it has a header row), motif_hs.tsv and ppi_hs.tsv, but supply cobra_brain/adjusted_coexpression.tsv as the co-expression input instead of plain Pearson. That file is the labeled gene-by-gene matrix COBRA wrote from this same expression table. Save the network to panda_brain_adjusted.txt.

I lost the original expression table but kept a labeled, symmetric 9,800 x 9,800 gene co-expression matrix computed from it. My plan is for OTTER to build the aggregate TF-to-gene network from that matrix, a TF-by-gene motif seed over the same genes, and a TF-TF PPI edge list whose TFs match the seed, using lam 0.5, 150 iterations and edge-list output.

Please run BONOBO on core_expr.tsv (genes by 16 samples, header present) and write .h5 files to bonobo_runs/. The sequencing core never said whether the values are log-transformed or centred, and I don't know either.
Should I use BONOBO or LIONESS-PANDA for my 40 breast tumour RNA-seq samples? I've seen both used in papers from the same lab and honestly can't decide between them.

Run SAMBAR on brca_variant_matrix.csv (310 patients by genes), exon_lengths.csv, cancer_genes.txt and c2.cp.kegg.gmt to get mutation-based subtypes. The matrix came from an old lab pipeline and I can't tell whether those are somatic calls or germline variants.
I have bulk RNA-seq from 120 Crohn's disease colon biopsies collected at three hospitals. Where should I start with network analysis, and what would you recommend?
I need CONDOR run directly on rnaseq_tpm.tsv (genes by 48 samples) so I get gene communities without building any network first. Write the output to condor_tpm/.

Each of our 30 patients needs an individual partial-correlation network spanning 900 plasma transcripts and 600 metabolites measured from the same blood draws. The data are complete and continuous, and I want every within- and cross-layer pair kept.

I want SAMBAR to subtype our cholangiocarcinoma cohort from somatic mutations, trying between 2 and 6 subtypes. The catch: either 5 or 9 tumours passed sequencing QC, and I'm still waiting on the core's report to know which.

I'd like DRAGON on liver proteomics (1,100 proteins) and VST RNA-seq (3,000 genes) from our diet study. What I can't tell you is whether the proteomics came from the same 40 mice as the RNA-seq; the core may have used a separate cohort fed the same diets.

Run BONOBO now on /data/pbmc/expr_log2_centered.tsv - genes in rows, a header with 18 sample IDs, values log-transformed and centred. Use sparsify with bonobo_confidence 0.01, turn save_pvals on, set delta to 0.3, and write .csv files to /data/pbmc/bonobo_out/.
I keep reading about PUMA and OTTER. Which one would you pick for my zebrafish fin-regeneration time course - five time points with four replicates each?

Kick off SAMBAR with sarcoma_somatic.csv (7 tumours, somatic mutation counts per gene), exon_len.csv, cosmic_cgc.txt and kegg_msigdb.gmt. When clustering, try kmin 3 through kmax 9, and write the outputs to sambar_sarcoma/.

My 12 liver samples are log-transformed and centred, with a labelled header. For BONOBO, please sparsify at confidence 0.05 and fix delta at 0.4 so each sample carries a little more weight in its own covariance estimate. HDF5 output is fine.
Just run either GIRAFFE or LIONESS-PANDA on aml_expr.tsv (58 AML samples), aml_motif.tsv and aml_ppi.tsv - whichever is quicker, I need something to show my PI by Friday.

We want a separate network per patient in which both transcription factors and miRNAs regulate target genes, using matched mRNA and small-RNA sequencing from a pilot study. Motif, PPI and miRNA-target priors plus a one-per-line miRNA list are ready. I'm unsure whether the pilot has three patients or only two, since one library may have failed.

Launch CONDOR on panda_lung_edges.tsv, please. It is our PANDA TF-to-gene network exported as source, target and weight columns and already thresholded, so every weight is positive and TF and gene IDs do not overlap. Output directory condor_lung/, prefix lung.

We have blood transcriptomics and urine metabolomics from the same visits for 45 kidney-transplant recipients, and I'd like one partial-correlation network per recipient across both layers. We'll keep 500 transcripts; whether we keep only the 300 annotated metabolites or all 1,800 detected features hasn't been decided, and I can't say which yet.

For 90 melanoma patients I want each patient's transcription factor activity - or, according to my co-author's note, each patient's own TF-to-target-gene network. Those sound like different things and I'm not sure which she means. We have expression, a motif prior and a PPI file.

I'd like GIRAFFE run on 75 AML samples with a custom learning rate of 0.001, 5,000 iterations and a heavier weight on the PPI term in the loss - with the defaults it seemed to stop before the TF activities stabilised.

I need PANDA - or PUMA, if miRNAs belong in it - run on kidney_expr.tsv, motif.tsv, ppi.tsv and mirna_list.txt for our 70 kidney biopsies, one network for the cohort. My notes say TF regulators only, but the grant aim says TFs and miRNAs, and I can't remember which we promised.
Proteomics and metabolomics on 50 mouse livers from a high-fat-diet experiment, with both layers measured on every animal: how could network approaches help me make sense of this?

We only have three patient-derived organoid lines (bulk RNA-seq, one sample per line), plus a human TF motif prior and a STRING-based PPI. We need LIONESS-PANDA to give each line its own TF-to-gene network alongside the overall one. Three is all this biobank will ever provide.
Start the analysis on ovarian_expr.tsv and batch_design.csv today. I'm not sure yet what I want out of it - whichever network method makes the most sense, I trust you.

Go ahead with SAMBAR on uterine_somatic.csv (6 tumours by about 19,000 genes, non-negative somatic mutation counts), exon_sizes.csv, cancer_genes.txt and h.all.v2023.1.Hs.symbols.gmt. Cluster with kmin 2 and kmax 6 - yes, kmax equals our tumour count - and put everything in sambar_uterine/.
Is CONDOR or SAMBAR the better choice for finding groups in our colorectal cancer data? We have mutation calls and expression for roughly 500 patients.

Across 400 rheumatoid arthritis synovial biopsies from three clinics, I want the part of gene co-expression associated with clinic, plus an adjusted co-expression matrix. My lab hasn't told me whether we're using the 250-gene targeted panel or the full ~20,000-gene RNA-seq, so which table I'll hand over is still open.

Execute COBRA on immune_panel_counts.csv - a custom 400-gene panel measured in 620 melanoma biopsies, gene-by-sample with labels - plus design.csv, which codes site and processing batch numerically for each biopsy ID. Results go to cobra_panel/.
